payload.review:
The dependency list changed materially this iteration, so this is a real review rather than a formality.

- typescript and @types/node: devDependencies, ordinary registry packages, no divergence, no ask. Reinstalled once mid-iteration when the shared install was destroyed, at the same pinned versions.
- kb (the benjamin module): WAS declared as an npm optionalDependency with a file: path protocol. That declaration is REMOVED. It was a second, redundant mechanism - the engine already resolves the module by PATH in modules.ts, read-only - and it was the mechanism that destroyed the imported repository. The module itself is unchanged in status: still an import, still resolved by path, still deactivating cleanly when the sibling checkout is absent. The import stamp on this iteration's grants reads kb: absent, which is honest - benjamin's working tree is currently empty pending the owner's re-clone.
- The vendored qrcode encoder (from i8c) is untouched here and remains vendored with attribution.

NEW ASK ANSWERED, by the owner during the iteration: an import is READ-ONLY, whatever the mechanism. That is a sticky ruling of the strongest kind - it is minted as se.law-imports-are-read-only and enforced by four mechanical checks, so no future dependency may be declared through a path protocol and nothing installed may resolve outside the repository. Every later ship inherits it without being asked again.

No dependency ships diverged.
payload.upstream:
One deposit owed and made, and one explicitly NOT pushed.

DEPOSITED: nothing to benjamin, because nothing was modified there - the damage was deletion, not divergence, and its content is recoverable from its own remote. The lesson that belongs upstream of this repository is the law itself, which lives in this ledger and travels with the module system rather than with benjamin.

NOT PUSHED, deliberately: the owner pushes. This iteration makes that more consequential than before, so the ship review's one standing message to the owner is that the push must now carry tags (--follow-tags). The iteration tag is the only handle on an iteration's record, and a plain push would send the live claims with nothing behind them. It is recorded as se.raid-tags-not-pushed with the owner as its owner, and taught in se.guidance-worktrees.
